_readme: STARTER TEMPLATE. Copy this to inventory.json, edit it to match the machines
you actually own, then run `npm run inventory:sync`.
Out of the box this assumes one thing: Ollama on this machine at its default
port. If you have that running, `check_health` goes green with no edits.
Everything else is disabled until you turn it on.

cloudEscalation.note: Cloud is strictly opt-in. While optIn is false, routing and fallback never select cloud hosts, even when every self-hosted lane is unreachable. Set optIn to true or export XX_STACK_ALLOW_CLOUD=1 to enable it.

limits: Best for low-latency coding and iterative execution

runtimes.notes: Ollama's default port. This is the one lane enabled out of the box — if `ollama serve` is running, the stack works with no edits.
Enable if you run llama-server locally on :8080.

services.notes: Optional self-hosted reader (ghcr.io/jina-ai/reader:oss): URL -> LLM-friendly markdown, preferred by research-deep's visit action when enabled. See xx-stack/runtime/READER-SERVICE-RUNBOOK.md. When absent or disabled, research degrades to plain fetch — never to a cloud reader.

network.notes: DELETE THIS MACHINE or replace it with a real one. Reached over Tailscale by MagicDNS name. Do not expose these ports publicly; bind them to the tailnet interface (find it with `tailscale ip -4` on the box) or firewall them to the tailnet.

limits: Prefer the OpenAI-compatible lane for long-context and high-throughput work

runtimes.notes: Example. sglang batches concurrent requests across GPUs, so parallel slices are cheap relative to sequential execution.
Example compatibility lane. Ollama binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and is not reachable over Tailscale until you set OLLAMA_HOST on the box and restart it.

aggregators.label: Hermes local-first control plane (loopback proxy)
aggregators.notes: OpenAI-compatible loopback proxy exposed by hermes-orchestration. Start it with `python3 hermes-orchestration/scripts/hermes_orchestrator.py serve` and export HERMES_PROXY_TOKEN. Enabling it delegates lane selection to Hermes instead of routing to a backend directly. Leave disabled if you would rather address machines directly — the two approaches are alternatives, not layers.

models.name: hermes-auto
models.notes: Virtual model name — Hermes resolves the real backend per its own lane policy.

providers.label: Generic OpenAI-compatible cloud endpoint
providers.notes: Template. Replace endpoint and models with a real provider if you opt in to cloud.
